title: Driving Test Prep: Road Signs & Rules
source: Common written driving-test topics: road signs, right-of-way, and basic traffic rules (right-hand-traffic countries such as the U.S.)

cards.prompt: In a right-hand-traffic country, a downward-pointing triangular sign with a red border and white background means the driver must:
distractors: Not enter the road at all
Slow to the posted speed limit
cards.explanation: Yield signs are triangular and stop signs are octagonal, so drivers can tell them apart by shape alone, even from an angle.

cards.prompt: In a right-hand-traffic country, at an all-way stop where two vehicles arrive at exactly the same time, which one has the right of way?
cards.explanation: This is the standard U.S. right-of-way rule for uncontrolled or all-way stop intersections.

cards.prompt: On a two-way road, what does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?
cards.answer: Passing (overtaking) is not allowed from your side of the road.

cards.prompt: On most road signs, a red circle with a diagonal line through a symbol means that action is {{prohibited}}.
In the U.S., what color are warning signs for general hazards such as sharp curves or falling rocks?
cards.explanation: Orange is reserved for temporary construction and work-zone signs, so it is kept distinct from general yellow warning signs.

cards.prompt: On a two-lane road, what must a driver do when approaching a school bus that has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm?
cards.answer: Stop completely and wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, regardless of direction of travel.

cards.prompt: Between two lanes moving in the same direction, what does a dashed (broken) white line indicate?
cards.answer: Lane changes are permitted when it is safe to do so.
distractors: Only buses may use this lane.

cards.prompt: A speed limit sign showing a number inside a white rectangle with a red border indicates the {{maximum}} speed allowed under normal conditions.
In the U.S., what shape is a stop sign, chosen so it can still be recognized even when its colors have faded?
cards.explanation: The unique octagon shape lets drivers recognize a stop sign by its outline alone, even from behind or in poor light.
